business_summary: Johnson & Johnson is a pure-play healthcare company run in two segments after the November 2023 spin-off of its consumer-health arm (Kenvue - Band-Aid, Tylenol, Listerine). What is left is: (1) Innovative Medicine, $60.401B of FY2025 sales (64% of the company), which invents, patents and sells prescription drugs in oncology (DARZALEX $14.351B, CARVYKTI $1.887B, ERLEADA $3.574B), immunology (TREMFYA $5.155B, STELARA $6.078B and falling fast), neuroscience (CAPLYTA, SPRAVATO, INVEGA), pulmonary hypertension, infectious disease and cardiovascular; and (2) MedTech, $33.792B of FY2025 sales (36%), which sells surgical instruments and sutures ($10.137B), orthopaedic implants ($9.258B), cardiovascular devices including electrophysiology catheters, Abiomed heart pumps and Shockwave ($8.928B) and contact lenses / eye-surgery products ($5.468B). Customers are hospitals, surgeons, wholesalers, pharmacies and government payers; drugs are sold on patent-protected pricing and devices on a razor/razor-blade model where surgeons who train on a platform keep buying its disposables. In 5-10 years the company should still be winning because it is the most diversified large-cap healthcare franchise in the world - no single drug is more than ~15% of sales, R&D of $14.665B a year (FY2025) refills the pipeline, the device business is protected by surgeon habit and hospital contracting, and the balance sheet (net debt ~$28B against ~$34B of normalized EBITDA) lets it buy innovation it does not invent. The catch is that the whole model is a treadmill: every drug eventually loses patent protection, so JNJ must keep replacing billions of lost revenue, and it carries a large, long-running talc-litigation liability from its former baby-powder business, on which it announced a proposed $5.5B settlement in July 2026.

moat.type: Patents and regulatory exclusivity in Innovative Medicine; surgeon switching costs, training lock-in and hospital contracting in MedTech; enormous scale in R&D, manufacturing and global distribution; brand/trust with physicians; 64 consecutive years of dividend increases signalling capital discipline

valuation.method: Blend of two methods, arithmetic done by code/valuation.py. (1) P/E: JNJ's own raised FY2026 adjusted-EPS guidance midpoint of $11.68 at 15x / 17.5x / 20x = $175.20 / $204.40 / $233.60. The base 17.5x is a deliberate premium to the drug-manufacturer median (~14.7x) for JNJ's diversification, AAA-grade balance sheet, 64-year dividend record and now-reduced talc tail risk - but below the ~23x the market pays today. (2) FCF yield: trailing-twelve-month FCF/share of $9.16 (derived from FY2025 10-K plus the 2026 and 2025 second-quarter 10-Qs) at target yields of 5.0% / 4.2% / 3.5% = $183.20 / $218.10 / $261.71. Average of the two bands gives low $179.20, base $211.25, high $247.66.

fair_value.method: pe(11.68 adj EPS @ 15/17.5/20x) + fcf_yield($9.16 TTM FCF/sh @ 5.0/4.2/3.5%), averaged

margin_of_safety_note: -0.2127 uses the formula (fair_value_base - price) / price = (211.25 - 268.31) / 268.31. Using the repo's own convention in code/valuation.py and code/thesis.py, (base - price) / base, the figure is -0.2701. Either way the number is negative: at $268.31 JNJ trades roughly 21-27% ABOVE our base fair value and above the high end of our band. There is no margin of safety here. This is a WATCH, not a BUY.
bull_case: Genuinely wide moat and unusual diversification: two segments, six therapeutic/device franchises, no single product above ~15% of sales, so one patent loss or one failed trial cannot break the company.

The growth engine is working. FY2025 sales grew 6.0% to $94.193B and Innovative Medicine grew 6.0% to $60.401B even while absorbing a 1,040 basis-point drag from the STELARA biosimilar cliff. Oncology grew 22.1% to $25.380B, led by DARZALEX +23.0% to $14.351B, CARVYKTI +95.9% to $1.887B and TREMFYA +40.5% to $5.155B.

Momentum accelerated in 2026: Q2 2026 sales $25.310B, up 6.6%, with Innovative Medicine +7.8% and MedTech +4.5%, and management raised FY2026 guidance to $100.8-101.4B of sales and $11.60-11.75 adjusted EPS (midpoint $11.68, up 8.2%).

High-quality economics: 67.9% gross margin, ~19% normalized ROIC, ~0.8x net-debt-to-EBITDA, and $19.698B of FY2025 free cash flow that comfortably covered $12.381B of dividends (63% of FCF) and $5.953B of buybacks.

The biggest overhang is being priced out: on 2026-07-27 JNJ announced an agreed comprehensive resolution of the ovarian talc litigation with the lead MDL and state-court plaintiff firms - a $5.5B commitment, first payment capped at $3B in 2027, nothing more due before 2028. That is a knowable, financeable number against ~$34B of annual EBITDA, versus a decade of open-ended uncertainty.
Owner-friendly and defensive: 64 consecutive years of dividend increases, $1.34 per quarter ($5.36 annualized, ~2.0% yield at $268.31), a business whose demand does not depend on the economic cycle.
risks: VALUATION IS THE MAIN RISK. At $268.31 the stock is ~23.0x the FY2026 adjusted-EPS guidance midpoint of $11.68 and ~29x trailing free cash flow (~3.4% FCF yield) for a business growing sales ~6% and adjusted EPS ~7-8%. The stock is up ~54% from its 52-week Alpaca low of $174.20, which was only ~14.9x the same guidance figure. Most of the last year's return has been multiple expansion, not earnings growth, and multiple expansion can reverse.

The talc settlement is NOT final. It is conditioned on participation by lead plaintiff firms representing at least 95% of the ~76,000 remaining ovarian claims. If that threshold is not met, JNJ goes back to trying cases one by one - a process that has already produced a >$1.5B mesothelioma verdict in Baltimore and a $40M Los Angeles ovarian verdict (and a defence win in June 2026). Three prior bankruptcy-based attempts to end this litigation all failed, most recently in March 2025.

An incremental talc charge is coming. The reserve stood at ~$3.7B present value at 2026-Q2, against a $5.5B commitment announced after the quarter closed, so a top-up charge should appear in Q3 2026 GAAP results. And the settlement excludes mesothelioma claims, state consumer-protection actions, Canadian litigation and an ongoing securities class action, so the tail does not close entirely.

The patent treadmill is relentless. STELARA fell 41.3% to $6.078B in FY2025 and is still bleeding; IMBRUVICA -7.1%, ZYTIGA -20.4%, INVEGA -9.8%. Under the Inflation Reduction Act, XARELTO and STELARA were on the first Medicare price-negotiation list effective 2026, and CMS added ERLEADA - a $3.574B, +19.2% grower - to the 2028 list in January 2026. Government price-setting is now a permanent, expanding headwind.

MedTech is the weaker half. It grew only 5.4% operationally in FY2025 and 3.6% operationally in Q2 2026, and earns a 12.2% pre-tax segment margin versus Innovative Medicine's 36.9%. Orthopaedics grew just 1.1%, Spine/Sports fell 2.5%, and China volume-based procurement plus pulsed-field-ablation competition in electrophysiology are real pressures.

Growth has been bought as much as built. JNJ spent $17.541B on acquisitions in FY2025 (Intra-Cellular, $14.5B net) and $15.146B in FY2024 (Shockwave). Intangibles plus goodwill are $99.175B of $199.210B total assets at FY2025 year-end - if pipeline assets disappoint, impairments follow and reported ROIC falls.

GAAP earnings are noisy and can mislead. FY2025 net income of $26.804B and diluted EPS of $11.03 were flattered by a ~$7.0B reversal of previously accrued talc reserves; FY2024's $5.79 was depressed by ~$5.1B of talc charges. Only the adjusted and cash figures are comparable year to year, and adjusted EPS itself excludes real intangible amortisation.
Concentration in US pricing policy, tariffs on pharmaceutical manufacturing, and FDA/regulatory outcomes are all outside management's control.
what_would_break_thesis: The proposed ovarian talc resolution fails to reach the required ~95% claimant participation and is abandoned or materially repriced, OR JNJ's total talc reserve rises above $10B.
Total company revenue declines year-over-year for two consecutive fiscal years.
Innovative Medicine segment sales decline year-over-year for two consecutive quarters on an operational (constant-currency) basis.
Company gross margin falls below 62% for two consecutive quarters.
Net-debt-to-EBITDA rises above 2.0x, or total debt exceeds $80B, without a clearly value-accretive acquisition behind it.
Free cash flow falls below $12B for a full fiscal year, or fails to cover the dividend in any fiscal year.
Normalized ROIC falls below 12% for two consecutive fiscal years.
The dividend is cut or the 60-plus-year increase streak is broken.
Goodwill and intangible impairments exceed $10B in any rolling two-year period (evidence that acquired growth was overpaid for).
Any accounting restatement, auditor change under dispute, or material governance red flag.

Price discipline trigger: do not buy above $211 (our base fair value). A first purchase only becomes justified at or below roughly $190 (about a 10% discount to base), and a full position below $179 (the low end of the band).
catalysts: Q3 2026 results, expected mid-October 2026 - the first report to quantify the incremental talc charge and to confirm the 95% claimant participation progress. This is important enough that the thesis should be refreshed early, before the 2026-12-10 refresh date, if results are materially different from guidance.
Formal court approval / confirmed 95% participation in the ovarian talc resolution would remove a decade-old discount but is, at today's price, arguably already assumed.
Continued Innovative Medicine acceleration as TREMFYA, DARZALEX, CARVYKTI, CAPLYTA, SPRAVATO and RYBREVANT/LAZCLUZE fully offset STELARA; management has targeted this as the pivot year.
MedTech re-acceleration - the OTTAVA robotic surgical system was submitted to the FDA in Q4 2025 and would be JNJ's entry against Intuitive Surgical.
A price pullback toward $190-211 would be the event that actually makes this ownable. A market-wide healthcare de-rating, a talc setback, or an IRA expansion scare are the plausible causes.
